• We handle piercings on the entire body, including earlobes, cartilage, and the body.
  • Is it painful to get your ears pierced? Can anesthesia be used?
  • How to choose your first piercing
  • Piercing procedure procedure
  • Care method until the piercing hole is completed
  • cost

We handle piercings on the entire body, including earlobes, cartilage, and the body.

At Norris Clinic, we handle piercings such as earlobe and cartilage piercings, belly button and body piercings.
You may also bring your own earrings of your choice. We also have a wide variety of earrings available for you to choose from.
We also have titanium earrings for people with metal allergies.

*If the earrings you have are not suitable for your first piercing, we may recommend ones available at our hospital.

Is it painful to get your ears pierced? Can anesthesia be used?

Especially if it's your first time, you may be worried about the "pain" when drilling the holes.
First, regarding earlobe piercings, at medical institutions, the piercing and fitting are done at the same time, so there is usually no pain. Even if it hurts, it only lasts for a moment. Therefore, anesthesia is generally not required. However, if you are really worried, we will use injection anesthesia.
On the other hand, in the case of body piercing, the piercing is generally done under anesthesia.

How to choose your first piercing

Use one with a long and thick shaft to securely fix it.

We recommend choosing one with a long and thick shaft so that it can be firmly fixed and the piercing hole completed.

Use materials with fewer impurities to prevent metal allergies

Choose earrings made of materials with few impurities, such as those made of medical grade stainless steel or those treated with pure gold.
In particular, for those with sensitive skin or those concerned about metal allergies, titanium and resin products are recommended.

Piercing procedure procedure

1counseling

The doctor will give you a consultation and discuss where to place the piercing, whether you have any allergies, etc.
If you are unsure whether you have allergies, we recommend an allergy test at a dermatologist.

2Deciding on your first piercing

You will choose your first piercing. You are welcome to bring your own piercings of your choice, but if they are not suitable for your first piercing, we recommend the piercings we have available at our clinic.

3Drilling and installation (anesthesia is also possible)

If necessary, anesthesia will be administered and the piercing will be done.

4Aftercare explanation

We will tell you how to care for you at home and you can go home.

Care method until the piercing hole is completed

For about 4 to 6 weeks, please take the following care when bathing. Detailed care instructions will be explained to you when you visit the hospital.

When taking a bath

  • Do not remove your earrings for a month and a half, then wash them with body soap, etc., and rinse them in the shower to keep them clean.
Precautions
  • Do not push the catch so hard that it tightens. Please maintain a slight gap on the catch side.
  • Please do not remove your first piercing until the piercing hole is completed (4 to 6 weeks).
  • Avoid getting hairspray, antiperspirant spray, perfume, etc. near the piercing hole.
  • Be careful not to get caught in your first piercing when putting on or taking off your clothes or tying your hair.
  • If you have a metal first piercing, please avoid saunas. Doing so may cause burns.
If you experience these symptoms, please visit the hospital again.
  • Pain, itching, swelling, and pus
  • There is a feeling of heat and swelling near the piercing hole.
  • A hard lump has formed in the piercing hole.
  • The area around the piercing hole has become red and swollen.

If you notice any other abnormalities, please do not touch the affected area and contact our hospital immediately.
